messages.content: How do I get a better crop of pepper?

Space for airflow and keep fruit off the soil to cut fungal losses. Pick regularly once fruit colours. Leaving ripe fruit on the plant slows further setting. Raise seedlings in a protected nursery and transplant when they are sturdy. Direct sowing gives an uneven stand.
Is it too late in the season to do that now?

Space for airflow and keep fruit off the soil to cut fungal losses. Pick regularly once fruit colours. Leaving ripe fruit on the plant slows further setting. Judge it against an untreated patch after a fortnight rather than by eye the next morning.
What goes wrong when farmers do not start beekeeping?

Site hives away from paths, livestock and homes, with shade and water within reach, because bees that must fly far for water work less and defend more. Harvest leaves enough honey for the colony to hold through the dearth period, and a colony stripped bare will abscond. Beekeeping fits well beside cropping, since the same bees improve pollination on nearby fields.

How do I plant soybean?

1. Rows about 50 to 75cm apart with plants close within the row, aiming for a dense even stand that shades out weeds.
2. Inoculating seed with rhizobium before planting is a small cost that raises nitrogen fixation and yield, especially on land that has not grown soybean before.
How do I plant oil palm?

1. About 9m triangular spacing, roughly 143 palms per hectare. Crowded palms shade each other and yield falls.
2. Plant tenera hybrid seedlings from a reputable source. Dura palms grown from random seed give much thicker shells and less oil.

How do I protect a sloping field from erosion?

On sloping land, ridge along the contour rather than up and down. Ridges running downhill become channels that concentrate water, and a channel becomes a gully within a season or two. Once a gully forms it takes far more work to repair than the ridging would have cost. Keeping the surface covered, with mulch or a cover crop, protects it from rain impact.
Why does it matter how I combine trees with my crops?

Trees kept deliberately in fields provide shade, fodder, fuel and, in the case of nitrogen fixing species, a real fertility contribution. The trade-off is competition for light and water, so choose species that come into leaf out of phase with the crop, and prune to manage the canopy. Done well the field carries both; done carelessly the trees win and the crop suffers.
I have half a hectare and almost no money this season. What is the single best thing I can do for my maize?

Weed on time. If you can only do one thing, that is the one.

Weeding costs labour rather than cash, and on a small maize plot it changes yield more than any input you could buy with the money you do not have. Maize is most vulnerable to competition in its first few weeks, so weeding early matters far more than weeding often.

After that, in order of how much they give back per naira spent:

1. Correct spacing and one plant per stand, which costs nothing but attention at planting.
2. Planting on established rains rather than the first shower, which avoids a replant.
3. If any cash exists, a small amount of nitrogen placed beside the plant at about three to four weeks, rather than broadcast. Placement makes a small quantity work like a larger one.

Avoid spending scarce money on spraying unless you have actually scouted and found a problem worth treating.

I am not sure when to put my leafy vegetables in the ground. Any guidance?

Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. Leafy types are cut repeatedly at intervals rather than harvested once, so soil fertility must be maintained through the cycle.
I think I have stem borers on my maize, sorghum, rice. How do I confirm it?

Stem borers on maize, sorghum, rice can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Deadheart in young plants, small holes in stems with frass, and tunnels when a stem is split open.

Destroy or plough in crop residues after harvest to break the carryover, since larvae overwinter in stalks. Early uniform planting across a community reduces pressure for everyone.
I want to keep backyard chickens profitably. What should I know?

Backyard flocks give the best return on very small capital, because the birds scavenge much of their own feed. The catch is that unvaccinated local flocks are periodically wiped out by Newcastle disease, which erases years of slow gains in a fortnight. Keeping vaccination up, and supplementing scavenging with a little grain, turns a fragile flock into a reliable one. Do the cheapest thing on this list first and give it two weeks before spending more.
How do I tell black sigatoka apart from other problems on plantain and banana?

Black sigatoka on plantain and banana can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Dark streaks that widen into blotches with pale centres, starting on older leaves and moving up.

Remove and destroy affected leaves, widen spacing for airflow, and keep the stool desuckered. Nutrition matters, since a well fed plant holds more functional leaves.
How do I use cover crops between seasons?

A cover crop over the off season protects the soil surface, adds organic matter and smothers weeds before they seed. Bare ground between seasons is a loss you do not see until yields drift down over several years. A legume cover adds nitrogen as well, which makes it close to free.

I think I have maize streak on my maize. How do I confirm it?

Maize streak on maize can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Fine broken pale streaks running parallel along the leaf, plants stunted when infected young.

Carried by leafhoppers, often from nearby grasses and volunteer maize. Tolerant varieties and avoiding very late or staggered planting near infected stands. There is no cure for an infected plant.
What is the right way to dry my harvest properly?

Dry on a tarpaulin or a raised platform, never on bare ground. Ground drying puts moisture back into the crop from below, adds soil and stones that buyers reject, and exposes it to animals. A raised platform also lets air move underneath, which dries faster and more evenly.

I farm in the guinea zone. What should I be growing?

Long single season, roughly 1000 to 1400mm. The maize, yam, soybean and rice belt. Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake.

How is groundnut grown?
Groundnut is a staple of West and Central African smallholder systems, known locally as epa (Yoruba), gyada (Hausa).

What is the right timing for cassava?

Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. 9 to 12 months for early varieties, up to 18 months for late. Roots left too long become woody and lose starch quality.
I want to handle cassava after harvest. What should I know?

Cassava roots deteriorate within about two days of lifting, so process within forty-eight hours rather than harvesting more than you can handle. Fermentation during processing into garri or fufu is also what lowers cyanogen levels, so it is a food safety step and not only a flavour one. Harvest in batches matched to your processing capacity.
When should I plant cassava?

Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. 9 to 12 months for early varieties, up to 18 months for late. Roots left too long become woody and lose starch quality. Keep a note of what you did and when, because next season that record beats any general advice.
What is the right way to dry produce faster and cleaner?

A simple raised solar dryer dries faster and cleaner than open ground, and keeps rain, dust and animals off the crop. Faster drying is directly less mould and less aflatoxin risk. It can be built from local timber and clear plastic sheet, and pays for itself in one rejected consignment avoided.
My goat has a fever, runny nose and sores in the mouth. Several others look sick too.

Fever with nasal discharge, mouth sores and rapid spread through a flock points at peste des petits ruminants. Act today, because it moves quickly and kills young stock hardest.

What to do now:

1. Separate visibly sick animals from the rest and handle the healthy ones first each time you go in.
2. Stop all movement in or out. Do not sell, lend or buy animals while this is running.
3. Contact your veterinary or extension officer today so the outbreak is known locally.
4. Bury or burn animals that die rather than leaving carcasses out.

Vaccination is the real control and it has to be in place beforehand. Once you have restocked, keep it up and quarantine every newly bought animal before it joins the flock.
What goes wrong when farmers do not dry produce faster and cleaner?

A simple raised solar dryer dries faster and cleaner than open ground, and keeps rain, dust and animals off the crop. Faster drying is directly less mould and less aflatoxin risk. It can be built from local timber and clear plastic sheet, and pays for itself in one rejected consignment avoided. Conditions differ between zones and soils, so treat this as a starting point.
Why does it matter how I decide which fertiliser to buy?

Buying fertiliser without testing is the most common way smallholders waste money. You pay for nutrients the soil already has while the one nutrient actually limiting your yield stays short, so the crop does not improve and the fertiliser gets blamed. A test costs far less than a season of the wrong input. Your extension officer will know where testing is available.

My groundnuts got rained on while drying. They look fine now that they are dry. Can I still sell them?

Be careful here, because looking fine is not the same as being safe.

Groundnut that dries slowly, or gets wetted again part way through drying, is the classic route to aflatoxin. It is a mould toxin, it is not visible at levels that still matter, and it does not go away once the nuts dry out. It causes real harm to people and animals, and it is the usual reason a consignment gets rejected at a formal buyer.

What I would do:

1. Sort hard. Discard every nut that is shrivelled, discoloured, mouldy or damaged. That sorting removes a large share of the risk.
2. Get them fully dry now and keep them dry, in ventilated storage off the ground.
3. If you are selling to a buyer who tests, ask about testing before you commit a large quantity.

For future harvests the defence is speed. Lift, dry fast on a tarpaulin or raised platform rather than bare ground, and get them under cover before rain. Once the toxin is there, there is nothing you can add to remove it.

How do I stop quelea and birds coming back next season?

1. Scaring must be sustained through the vulnerable window from grain fill to harvest. Community wide timing works far better than one farmer acting alone, because birds simply move next door.

Keep a note of what you did and when, because next season that record beats any general advice.
How is sorghum and millet grown?
Sorghum and millet are staples of West and Central African smallholder systems, known locally as dawa (sorghum, Hausa), gero (millet, Hausa).

What is the right way to know when grain is dry enough to store?

Grain must be dry enough before storage, around thirteen percent moisture, or it will heat, mould and be eaten by insects whatever else you do. Grain that feels dry in the afternoon sun is often still too wet, because the surface dries faster than the inside. Bite tests and the sound of grain poured into a tin are rough guides; a moisture meter at a co-operative is better.

What goes wrong when farmers do not stock my broiler house?

Overcrowding is the most common avoidable mistake in a small broiler house. Too many birds in the space raises litter moisture, which raises ammonia, which damages the birds' airways and opens the door to disease. Growth slows and mortality rises even when feed is good. If the litter is wet and the house smells sharp when you walk in, you are overstocked or under-ventilated.
I have been having stomach pain for three days. What should I take?

That is outside what I can help with. I advise on farming, not on human health, and I am not able to tell you what to take.

Please see a health worker or clinic about pain that has lasted three days.

If you came here with a farm question as well, I am glad to help with that.
What goes wrong when farmers do not package produce for market?

Packaging is not decoration. Grading produce into uniform sizes and packing it cleanly gets a better price for exactly the same crop, because buyers pay for predictability and reject lots they must sort themselves. It also reduces damage in transit, so more of what you grew arrives saleable.

How I go keep my maize make weevil no chop am?

Two thing dey decide am, and the first one na the one people dey skip.

1. Dry am well first. If the maize never dry reach, nothing you do after go work. Maize wey feel dry for afternoon sun fit still wet too much for storage. Dry am for tarpaulin or raised platform, no be for bare ground, because ground go put water and sand back inside.

2. Use hermetic bag like PICS. The bag dey block air so the weevil no fit breathe, and you no need chemical at all. But e only work if you tie the inside liner well every single time you open am. If you leave am loose, na ordinary bag be dat.

Check the store sometimes. If you see hole for the grain or dust for under the bag, weevil don enter.
My cocoa is showing damage and I suspect cocoa black pod. How do I be sure?

Cocoa black pod on cocoa can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Dark brown to black spreading lesions on pods, often starting at the tip or stalk end, in wet weather.

Harvest frequently, remove and bury or destroy infected pods, prune for an open canopy and improve drainage. Sanitation does most of the work.

What is the right way to plan a rotation?

Alternating legumes and cereals does two things at once: it breaks pest and disease cycles that build up under continuous cropping, and it leaves nitrogen behind for the following cereal. A cowpea or soybean crop before maize measurably reduces next season's fertiliser bill. Continuous maize on the same ground is what invites striga and stem borer to establish.
How do I avoid aflatoxin in groundnut and maize?

Aflatoxin is a mould toxin, worst in groundnut and maize, produced when drying is slow or storage is damp. It is invisible at levels that still cause harm, it does not go away once formed, and it gets consignments rejected by any buyer who tests. The defences are practical: lift and dry fast, never let a drying crop get rained on, and sort out every shrivelled, discoloured or mouldy nut before storage. Your local extension officer can confirm which varieties and products are registered in your area.
How do I cure cassava mosaic once the plants already have it?

You cannot. I would rather tell you that than sell you a step that does nothing.

It is a virus. There is no spray, no drench and no fertiliser that reverses it in a plant that is already infected. Anyone offering you one is taking your money.

What you can do:

1. Rogue out the worst affected plants so they stop acting as a source.
2. Accept this season's crop for what it is.
3. Fix it at the source for next season: take cuttings only from healthy vigorous plants, and get a resistant variety if one is available near you.

Farmers who change that one habit, where their planting material comes from, stop having this problem.

My cassava leaf dey yellow and e twist. I don spray insecticide but nothing change.

Make you stop to spend money for spray. Na cassava mosaic disease be dat, and no insecticide fit cure am.

Na virus. Whitefly dey carry am, but the main way e dey enter na through the stem wey you plant. If you cut your stem from plant wey get the sickness, the farm don carry am before e even germinate. Na why the spray no do anything.

Wetin you go do:

1. This season own don happen. Comot the plant wey bad well well.
2. This one important: no ever cut planting stem from plant wey dey show this sign. Cut from healthy strong plant, from the middle of stem wey don reach eight to twelve months.
3. Try get improved variety like TME 419 or TMS 30572 wey fit resist am.

Clean planting material na the whole control.

My cassava yield is poor. How do I improve it?

1. Weed control in the first 3 months determines yield more than any other single factor, because cassava canopies late and cannot compete early.
2. 1m by 1m for sole crop, about 10,000 plants per hectare. Wider at 1m by 1.5m when intercropping with maize.
3. Improved varieties such as TME 419, TMS 30572 and TMS 98/0505 offer mosaic resistance and higher root yield than most local landraces.

Check this against what your neighbours are seeing before you act on a whole field.
Which fertiliser should I buy for my farm?

I cannot answer that honestly without knowing what your soil is short of, and that is exactly the point.

Buying fertiliser without testing is the most common way smallholders waste money. You end up paying for nutrients the soil already has, while the one nutrient that is actually limiting your yield stays short. The crop does not improve and the fertiliser gets blamed.

What I would suggest:

1. Get a soil test if there is any facility within reach. Your extension officer will know where. The cost is small against a season of the wrong fertiliser.
2. While you wait, improve what does not need a test: organic matter, crop rotation with a legume, and correct placement.
3. When you do apply, place or band fertiliser beside the plant rather than broadcasting it. Broadcast urea on hot dry ground loses a large share to the air before the plant ever sees it.

If testing genuinely is not possible, tell me your crop, your zone and what you grew on that land last season, and I can give you a reasonable starting point.
My stored grain and legumes is showing damage and I suspect storage pests. How do I be sure?

Storage pests on stored grain and legumes can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Boreholes in grain, dust beneath the bag, live insects when the surface is disturbed.

Dry thoroughly to safe moisture before storage, then use hermetic bags such as PICS that suffocate insects without chemicals. Sealing discipline is what makes hermetic bags work.
Can you explain leafy vegetables farming for a beginner?

Leafy vegetables are staples of West and Central African smallholder systems, known locally as ugu / fluted pumpkin, tete / amaranth, ewedu / jute mallow, ila / okra. Leafy types are cut repeatedly at intervals rather than harvested once, so soil fertility must be maintained through the cycle. Short cycle leafy vegetables turn over in weeks, which makes them the practical way to generate cash between long season crops.
What is the best approach to cassava mosaic?

The main control is clean planting material and resistant varieties. Rogue out badly affected plants. There is no spray that cures an infected plant. Yellow and green mottling, distorted and reduced leaves, stunted plants. Carried by whitefly and, most importantly, by planting infected stem cuttings.
I already did that and it did not help. What else?

The main control is clean planting material and resistant varieties. Rogue out badly affected plants. There is no spray that cures an infected plant. Yellow and green mottling, distorted and reduced leaves, stunted plants. When a problem returns each season the source was usually never removed, rather than the treatment having failed.

My chickens are dying suddenly. Many died in two days. Some have twisted necks.

Sudden high mortality with twisted necks and nervous signs points strongly to Newcastle disease. Act today, because it moves fast through a flock.

What to do now:

1. Separate the birds still looking healthy from the sick ones immediately, and handle the healthy group first each time you go in.
2. Stop all movement of birds in or out. Do not sell or give away birds from this flock, and do not bring replacements in yet.
3. Dispose of dead birds by burying or burning them. Do not leave carcasses where other birds or animals reach them.
4. Contact your veterinary or extension officer today so the outbreak is known about locally.

There is no treatment that cures Newcastle once a flock breaks with it. Vaccination is the only real control, and it has to be in place before an outbreak, on schedule. Once you have restocked, keep the vaccination programme up, quarantine every new or returning bird before mixing, and never bring unsold birds back from the market straight into the flock.
How do I use poultry manure safely?

Poultry manure is strong and fast acting, which cuts both ways. Fresh manure burns young plants and carries weed seed, so compost or age it before use. Applied well ahead of planting and worked in, it feeds the crop and builds organic matter at the same time, which bagged fertiliser does not do.
Can you explain cocoa farming for a beginner?

Cocoa is a staple of West and Central African smallholder systems. Harvest ripe pods regularly rather than in occasional large sweeps. Frequent harvest removes disease sources and reduces losses. Fermentation and drying decide the price you are paid. Under-fermented or smoke-tainted beans are downgraded no matter how good the tree was.
How do I get a better crop of cocoa?

Prune to keep the canopy open and remove chupons and dead wood. An open canopy dries faster and suffers less black pod. Young cocoa needs shade to establish. Mature trees tolerate more light, but full sun without adequate nutrition shortens the life of the farm. Harvest ripe pods regularly rather than in occasional large sweeps. Frequent harvest removes disease sources and reduces losses. Fermentation and drying decide the price you are paid. Under-fermented or smoke-tainted beans are downgraded no matter how good the tree was.
I already did that and it did not help. What else?

Prune to keep the canopy open and remove chupons and dead wood. An open canopy dries faster and suffers less black pod. Young cocoa needs shade to establish. Mature trees tolerate more light, but full sun without adequate nutrition shortens the life of the farm. Something carries it between seasons. Find that and the treatment starts working.
